episodes.about: Google's Gemini 4 Argon has landed with mixed coding reviews but impressive visual demos and a surprising strength in writing; the host works out where the new model actually fits.
episodes.title: What Gemini 4 Argon Is Actually Good For
episodes.why: Google's new flagship landed this week - this is the clearest-eyed take on what it is actually good at, in 30 minutes.

episodes.about: What happens when AI agents stop recommending purchases and start making them: the infrastructure for safely giving agents payment credentials, agentic tokens, wallets competing to become the agent payment layer, and who is liable when an agent makes a mistake.
episodes.title: When AI Agents Start Spending Your Money | Alex Rampell & Terry Angelos
episodes.why: Agents are starting to hold payment credentials. Rampell is a payments guy, so this is the infrastructure view, not the hype view.

episodes.about: A man named Mike Smith was sentenced to 18 months in prison and fined over $8 million for building an AI system that faked billions of streams and earned millions in royalties; Wired's Kate Knibbs explains how he pulled it off, how he got caught, and what it means for the internet's AI slop problem.
episodes.title: The $8 million AI music scam
episodes.why: A man built an AI streaming-fraud machine, made millions, and got 18 months. A great story that also explains the AI slop economy.

episodes.about: Meta just shipped smart glasses with no camera, and Amazon's Bee wearable is always listening - what do we do in a world where everything might be recording, and can tech companies make that feel okay?
episodes.title: Everything's recording everybody. What now?
episodes.why: The closest of today's five to daily life - always-on AI wearables are arriving now, not in some future keynote.

episodes.about: Leash Bio uses DNA Encoded Libraries to generate extremely high-throughput protein-small-molecule interaction data ideal for large-scale ML modeling; the episode also covers their new Minos playground, which turns that data into tens of thousands of lab-in-the-loop simulations for training agents in verifiable scientific reasoning - released the same day with a preprint and open dataset.
episodes.title: Lab-in-the-Loop at Compute Speed - Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
episodes.why: The deep cut: ML trained on millions of real lab experiments, with the dataset released the same day. Long - save it for a drive.
